slides.stem: If $a^{2/5} = 9$, where $a > 0$, what is the value of $a^{6/5}$?

slides.intro: Notice $\frac{6}{5} = 3 \times \frac{2}{5}$, so cube what you already have.
slides.trapWhy: $27$ multiplies $9 \times 3$. Raising a power to a power multiplies exponents, not values.

slides.title: Build the exponent you need
slides.body:
When you know $a^n$ and the question wants $a^m$, write $m$ as a multiple of $n$: then $a^m = (a^n)^k$.

Solving for $a$ itself means fifth roots and decimals. The ladder skips all of it.
